question: C is four times as efficient as D. C takes 63 days less than D to complete a work. If both of them work together, then in how many days will the same work be completed?
solution:
**Given:**

C is four times as efficient as D.

C takes 63 days less than D to complete a work.

**Formula Used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

If C is 4 times as efficient as D, let efficiency of D be 1 unit, then efficiency of C = 4 units.

If D takes x days to complete the work, then C takes (x - 63) days to complete the work.

When both work together, their combined efficiency = Efficiency of C + Efficiency of D.

Time taken = Work / Combined Efficiency.
